experiences.label: The Little-City Experience
experiences.tagline: Small cities, a garage at most buildings, a longer drive to your parents.

story.title: The Little-City Experience
story.text: A garage at most buildings, and often a small downtown nearby.

story.title: A weekday
story.text: From the typical apartment a park is about 8 minutes on foot and the supermarket about 0.4 miles. A public dog park is about 1.1 miles from the typical apartment.

story.title: Saturday night
story.text: You can usually walk to dinner: about 7 restaurants are within a 10-minute walk of the typical apartment. Bars are usually few, so a late night means a ride.

story.title: Sunday with Mom and Dad
story.text: Seeing your parents is a planned trip from most of these towns. Tolls run up to about $41 round trip with a New York E-ZPass, and the train and bus take about 106 minutes.

story.title: What it costs
story.text: Rent is typically about $1,830 a month. With utilities and fees the total is typically about $2,050.

story.title: The catch
story.text: From here you usually cannot drop in on your parents. The typical apartment is also modest in size, about 590 square feet.

experiences.label: The Old-Neighborhood Experience
experiences.tagline: An older city neighborhood: close to your parents, except in Newark.

story.title: The Old-Neighborhood Experience
story.text: Errands on foot in a long-established city neighborhood.

story.title: A weekday
story.text: A dog run is about 1.2 miles from the typical apartment. About 3 cafés are close for a break from the desk, and the supermarket is about 0.2 miles away.

story.title: Saturday night
story.text: Dinner is easy, with about 71 restaurants within 1 mile of the typical apartment. Bars are usually few, so a late night often means going to another neighborhood.

story.title: Sunday with Mom and Dad
story.text: From Brooklyn, Queens and Manhattan your parents are close enough for a weeknight visit. From Newark the drive is about 47 minutes each way. The typical trip by train and bus takes about 60 minutes.

story.title: What it costs
story.text: Rent is typically about $1,900 a month. With utilities and fees the total is typically about $2,163.

story.title: The catch
story.text: Nightlife and easy parking are usually what you give up. Bars are usually few, and many of these buildings do not list a garage.

experiences.label: The Room-to-Breathe Experience
experiences.tagline: Usually more space for you, the desk and the dog, in towns farther out.

story.title: The Room-to-Breathe Experience
story.text: Usually more room for you, your desk and the dog.

story.title: A weekday
story.text: Most of these apartments have room for a proper desk. From the typical apartment a park is about 9 minutes on foot, and the supermarket is about 0.8 miles away.

story.title: Saturday night
story.text: From the typical apartment about 10 restaurants are within 1 mile, and bars are usually scarce. With this much space, having friends over is an easy evening.

story.title: Sunday with Mom and Dad
story.text: Seeing your parents is a long drive from most of these towns. Tolls run up to about $47 round trip with a New York E-ZPass, and the train and bus take about 107 minutes.

story.title: What it costs
story.text: Rent is typically about $1,805 a month. With utilities and fees the total is typically about $2,044.

story.title: The catch
story.text: From most of these towns your parents are a long drive away. The typical apartment has only about 4 restaurants within a 10-minute walk.
